hero.lead: The complete path, from your first git --version to a Pull Request approved by the team. Written for data analysts and Power BI developers who have never used Git — and who need to stop emailing .pbix files around.
hero.caption: The path you will follow in this guide: the project is born in Power BI Desktop, edited in VS Code, versioned by Git, shared on GitHub and reviewed by the team.
sec.introducao.lead: Before typing a single command, it helps to understand what each piece does. These are four independent tools that, together, solve the most common problem on any BI team: knowing which version of the report is the right one.
sec.instalacao.lead: Six steps, once per machine. By the end of this chapter your computer will be ready to version any Power BI project.
sec.pbip-versionado.lead: Now the project stops being a "loose file" and gains history. It takes four steps: open it in VS Code, initialize Git, create the .gitignore and make the first commit.
sec.repositorio.lead: The history already exists on your machine. Now it needs an address in the cloud so the whole team can reach the same project.
sec.clone.lead: git clone downloads the project and its entire history to a new machine. It is a first-time operation — and this is where many people get confused.
sec.workflow.lead: This is the cycle you will repeat every day. Six steps, always in the same order. Learn this chapter by heart and everything else becomes detail.
sec.branches.lead: A branch is an independent line of work. It lets you experiment, break things and start over without touching the report that is live in production.
sec.pull-request.lead: A Pull Request (PR) is a formal request: "I finished my part, please review it and bring it into the project". This is where peer review happens — and where PBIP proves its worth.
sec.merge.lead: Merge is the operation that brings commits from one branch into another. Git tries to do it on its own — and it succeeds most of the time.
sec.conflitos.lead: A conflict is not an error or a defect: it is Git telling you that two people had different ideas about the same line. Resolving it means choosing — and testing.
sec.colaboracao.lead: Let's put it all together in a real scenario: two analysts, one project, one week of work. Ana owns the semantic model; Bruno owns the visuals.
sec.boas-praticas.lead: Eight simple agreements that turn Git from "the tool that gets in the way" into a process the team no longer notices.
sec.publicacao.lead: The business has approved the project. Now the change has to travel the last stretch: from develop to main, and from main to the Power BI Service.
sec.comandos.lead: The quick reference to keep at hand. Thirteen commands cover more than 95% of the work on a Power BI project.
sec.checklist.lead: Check each item as you go. Your progress is saved in your browser, so you can close the page and come back later.
